If you're anything like me, you've probably spent far too much time on Wikipedia, clicking from one article to the next, going deeper and deeper down the rabbit hole. Now there's finally an official app… or rather, a widget for that.

Finally, there's a button that lets you open a random Wikipedia article.

Today's update to the Wikipedia iOS app introduces a rather fun and practical new feature: a "Random Article" widget that can be placed on the home screen of your iPhone or iPad.

The widget comes in both small and medium sizes, and even includes a cute mascot.

Tap the widget and you'll be taken straight to a completely random Wikipedia article, with "Random Mode" automatically enabled.

You don't need to leave the app and tap the widget again — just hit the random button and it'll roll the dice for you, keeping you going deeper and deeper down that random rabbit hole.

Have fun, but try not to lose track of time! Speaking of which, the Wikipedia app added a history trivia game earlier this summer.

The brand-new widget is available in today's update of the Wikipedia iPhone and iPad apps.

Make the most of your Apple devices.
